udp_verify.title: Important Information: UDP Output
udp_verify.intro: The UDP (User Datagram Protocol) protocol is recommended for local networks due to its low latency, but has specific characteristics:
udp_verify.stability_desc: UDP has no packet retransmission. If the network fluctuates, there will be visible "drops". SRT is preferred for remote access.
udp_verify.network_desc: Not recommended for UDP (use SRT). If necessary, it requires Port Forwarding on the router (Port 1234 UDP).
udp_verify.sync_desc: Our PUSH manageable system starts and continuously feeds the firewall natively, eliminating handshake latencies and common initial broadcast errors.
udp_verify.firewall_warning: * Make sure the server firewall allows traffic on the chosen port.

logs.title: System Diagnostics
logs.intro: Real-time monitoring of channel health and playout logs.
logs.schedule_validity: Checks if the current channel has a valid playlist for the current time.
logs.active_protocols: List of enabled distribution protocols (RTMP, SRT, etc.).
logs.last_logs: Latest technical output from the encoder.

active_channel.title: Active Channel Context
active_channel.desc: All operations in this dashboard (Start/Stop, Skip, Toggles) apply ONLY to the channel selected in the sidebar.

multi_channel.title: Multi-Channel
multi_channel.intro: Manage multiple playout channels simultaneously from a single interface. Each channel operates independently with its own playback engine.

management.title: Channel Management
management.intro: Create and delete channels according to your broadcast needs.
management.create_desc: Click the '+' button to add a new channel. Each channel requires a unique name and will be initialized with the system's default settings.
management.delete_desc: Select the channel you want to remove and click the delete icon. The channel must be stopped before it can be deleted.
management.default_desc: The main channel (main) is always preserved and cannot be deleted. This channel is used as the main reference for the system.

status.title: Channel States
status.intro: Each channel can be in one of the following states:
status.playing_desc: The channel is currently broadcasting content. The current clip is playing and the uptime counter is active.
status.paused_desc: Playback has been temporarily paused. The content remains visible but does not advance. Uptime continues to count.
status.stopped_desc: The channel is inactive and not broadcasting. The uptime is reset and no content is playing.
status.error_desc: A problem occurred with the channel playback. Check the system logs for more details on the error.

preview.title: Preview
preview.intro: View each channel's content in real-time through HLS streams.
preview.hls_desc: Each channel generates an HLS stream that can be viewed directly in the browser. The URL is automatically generated for each channel.
preview.safari_desc: Safari has native HLS support. Simply click the preview icon to open the native player.
preview.chrome_desc: These browsers require the hls.js library to play HLS streams. The system automatically loads it when needed.

info.title: Channel Information
info.currentClip_desc: Name of the media clip currently playing on this channel.
info.nextUp_desc: Name of the next clip in the playlist that will play after the current clip.
info.uptime_desc: Time elapsed since the channel entered 'Playing' state (HH:MM:SS format).
info.bitrate_desc: Current bitrate of the output stream in Mbps (megabits per second).

controls.title: Channel Controls
controls.intro: Control buttons available for each channel:
controls.play_desc: Starts or resumes channel playback. The channel changes to 'Playing' state.
controls.stop_desc: Stops playback immediately. The channel changes to 'Stopped' state.
controls.skip_desc: Advances immediately to the next clip in the playlist, regardless of the current clip's progress.

tips.title: Tips and Recommendations
tips.content:
• Each additional channel requires system resources (CPU, memory). On systems with limited resources, it is recommended to limit to 2-3 simultaneous channels.
• The main channel is always automatically created at system startup.
• Use the preview function to check broadcast quality before making it available to the public.
• In case of persistent errors, check the network connection and system logs in the Diagnostics section.

masterDashboard.title: Master Dashboard
masterDashboard.intro: The Master Dashboard provides a real-time mosaic monitoring of all active channels in the system.

mosaic.title: Mosaic Grid
mosaic.desc: Displays low-latency HLS previews. A red 'LIVE' badge indicates the channel is currently broadcasting.

context.title: Switching Context
context.desc: Clicking on any channel brick will set it as the 'Active Channel' and navigate you to the main Dashboard for detailed control.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.intro: The Dashboard is the main operational page of the playout. From here you control everything happening in real-time.

status_indicator.title: ON AIR / OFF AIR Indicator
status_indicator.prefix: At the top of the Dashboard there is a broadcast status indicator:

controls.title: Start / Stop Playout
controls.step1: Verify you have a playlist scheduled for the current time in the Calendar.
controls.step2: Click START — the system automatically validates the schedule before starting.
controls.step3: Choose protocols to activate (RTMP, SRT, UDP) and click 'Start Engine'.
controls.step4: The LIVE PREVIEW monitor shows the broadcast after 6-10 seconds (HLS time).
controls.step5: To stop, click STOP. All protocols are automatically disconnected.
controls.warning: If there is no scheduled playlist, the playout won't start. Configure the calendar first.

protocols.title: Broadcast Protocols
protocols.intro: The system supports multiple simultaneous protocols:
protocols.rtmp: Ideal for social media (YouTube/FB) and CDNs.
protocols.udp: Protocol for local networks and IP encoders.
protocols.others: Adaptive HTTP formats and Web streaming.

clips.title: Clip Visualization
clips.intro: In the Playlist tab you can see the status of each clip:
clips.skip: Skip current clip and move to next.

logs.title: Monitoring (Engine Logs)
logs.intro: Technical info extracted directly from the playout engine:

library.title: Media Library
library.intro: Central repository for all videos, audios and other content.

upload.title: Upload Videos
upload.step1: Click UPLOAD or drag files to the drop area.
upload.step2: Supported formats: MP4, MOV, MKV, AVI, TS, MXF (H.264/H.265).
upload.step3: The system automatically extracts metadata (duration, resolution, codec).
upload.step4: A thumbnail is automatically generated from the center frame.
upload.nfs_hint: Tip: Network folders (NFS/SMB) are automatically detected if configured.

metadata.intro: Every uploaded file is analyzed to extract technical and editorial details.
metadata.auto_review: The system automatically reviews metadata of uploaded clips.

fillers.title: Fillers
fillers.desc: Fillers are clips used to fill gaps in the schedule or as emergency content when no playlist is active.

syncFolder.title: Watchfolder Sync
syncFolder.desc: The Sync Watchfolder button scans the physical directory associated with the ACTIVE CHANNEL and registers new media files. It does not affect other channels.

playlists.title: Playlist Editor
playlists.intro: Playlists are sequences of content that the playout engine reproduces in order.

create.title: Create a Playlist
create.step1: Go to the Playlists menu and click 'New Playlist'.
create.step2: Assign an identifying name (e.g., Morning Movies).
create.step3: Drag clips from the Media Library to the right list.
create.step4: Reorder clips by dragging them up or down.
create.step5: Click SAVE to register the playlist.

management.title: Playlist Management
management.sorting_desc: Click arrow icons or drag to change order.
management.remove_clip_desc: Click the trash icon to remove a single clip.
management.duplicate_desc: Create copies of existing playlists for quick variations.
management.total_duration_desc: The system calculates total duration in real-time.
management.fillers_desc: Clips identified as fillers are ignored in base calculation but used in broadcast.

best_practices.title: Best Practices
best_practices.bullets:
• Avoid playlists longer than 24 hours.
• Validate if all clips have thumbnails.
• Use descriptive names for easier scheduling.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.intro: The calendar is where you schedule your broadcast.

schedule.title: Schedule a Playlist
schedule.step1: Click on a day in the calendar to open the scheduling dialog.
schedule.step4: Choose the repetition pattern: None, Daily, Weekly, or Monthly.
schedule.step5: Click SAVE. The event appears on the calendar with the corresponding color.

graphics.title: Graphic Editor
graphics.intro: The Graphic Editor allows you to create and manage visual overlays, logos and animated layers for your live broadcasts.
graphics.features_intro: The Graphic Editor offers professional tools for broadcast graphics production:
graphics.feature1: Precise logo and graphics positioning with multiple anchor point support
graphics.feature2: Full control of scale, opacity and rotation for each graphic element
graphics.feature3: Layer system to organize complex overlays with individual control
graphics.feature4: Integration with template library for quick design reuse
graphics.feature5: Support for multiple layers of text, images, shapes and animations
graphics.position_tab_intro: Control the exact position of graphic elements on the broadcast screen.
graphics.anchor_point_desc: Select one of 4 corners (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) as positioning reference.
graphics.offset_x_desc: Fine-tune horizontal position in pixels (0-1920). Use the slider or drag the logo in the preview.
graphics.offset_y_desc: Fine-tune vertical position in pixels (0-1080). Use the slider or drag the logo in the preview.
graphics.drag_drop_desc: Drag the logo directly in the preview area for intuitive real-time positioning.
graphics.style_tab_intro: Adjust visual properties like size and transparency of graphic elements.
graphics.scale_desc: Controls the logo size (10%-300%). The value represents the percentage of the output screen width.
graphics.opacity_desc: Controls the element transparency (10%-100%). Values below 80% are recommended for non-intrusive overlays.
graphics.layer_tab_intro: Create and manage multiple overlapping graphic layers. Each layer can be of a different type.
graphics.layer_clock_desc: Displays a real-time digital clock with customizable format, timezone and style.
graphics.layer_lower_third_desc: Text banner with title and subtitle, ideal for presenter identification or information.
graphics.layer_marquee_desc: Horizontal scrolling text with configurable speed and direction, ideal for breaking news.
graphics.clock_config_intro: Customize the appearance and behavior of the clock layer.
graphics.clock_format_desc: Choose between 24h (HH:mm:ss) or 12h (hh:mm:ss AM/PM), with or without seconds.
graphics.clock_timezone_desc: Select the timezone for display. Includes all world regions organized by continent.
graphics.clock_font_desc: Choose the typography: Roboto Mono, Inter, Courier New or Arial.
graphics.clock_size_desc: Set the font size in pixels. Recommended: 48px for large screens.
graphics.clock_color_desc: Select the clock text color using the color picker.
graphics.clock_bg_desc: Set the background color in RGBA format. Ex: rgba(0,0,0,0.7) for semi-transparent background.
graphics.lower_third_config_intro: Customize the text banner that appears at the bottom of the screen.
graphics.lt_primary_desc: Main name or title that appears highlighted in the banner.
graphics.lt_secondary_desc: Subtitle or complementary description that appears below the primary text.
graphics.lt_animation_desc: Choose the entry effect: Slide In Left, Slide In Right, Fade In or None.
graphics.lt_duration_desc: Time in milliseconds that the lower third remains visible before disappearing.
graphics.marquee_config_intro: Customize the scrolling text that appears on the broadcast screen.
graphics.marquee_text_desc: Enter the text to be displayed as a scrolling crawler. Supports multiple lines.
graphics.marquee_speed_desc: Controls the scrolling speed in pixels per second. Higher values = faster scrolling.
graphics.marquee_direction_desc: Choose the scrolling direction: Left to Right or Right to Left.
graphics.templates_tab_intro: Access and manage saved templates for quick reuse of predefined graphic configurations.
graphics.how_to_intro: Follow these steps to use the Graphic Editor effectively:
graphics.step1: Access the Graphic Editor through the Graphics menu in the sidebar
graphics.step2: Use the "Positioning" tab to define the exact location of your logo on screen
graphics.step3: Adjust scale and opacity in the "Style" tab to achieve the desired appearance
graphics.step4: In the "Layers" tab, click "Add Layer" and choose the type (Clock, Lower Third or Marquee)
graphics.step5: Configure each layer individually by clicking the edit icon
graphics.step6: Reorder layers by dragging them to define the overlay order
graphics.step7: Preview your changes in real-time on the 16:9 preview monitor
graphics.step8: Click "Save Changes" to apply the settings to your playout
graphics.tips_content:
• Use anchor points to maintain relative positioning when resizing the screen
• Keep opacity below 80% for non-intrusive overlays
• Organize layers by importance (background → overlays → text)
• Save frequent configurations as templates for quick reuse
• Always preview in full screen to verify the final appearance
• Use contrasting colors to ensure readability in different lighting conditions
• Enable/disable layers individually to test different compositions
• Use the clock with correct timezone for international broadcasts

settings.title: System Settings
settings.intro: The Settings menu allows you to configure all aspects of the playout system, from transmission protocols to user management.
settings.features_intro: The Settings menu offers complete tools for system management:
settings.feature1: Transmission protocol configuration (RTMP, SRT, UDP, HLS)
settings.feature2: Storage paths and metadata APIs management
settings.feature3: Playout engine configuration and quality presets
settings.output_tab_intro: Configure transmission protocols and video output parameters.
settings.primary_protocol_desc: Select the main protocol: RTMP, SRT, UDP or HLS.
settings.multi_streaming_desc: Enable additional protocols for simultaneous transmission.
settings.connection_links_desc: Direct links for VLC, OBS and other players.
settings.paths_tab_intro: Configure storage paths and metadata APIs.
settings.storage_paths_desc: Define directories for media, thumbnails, playlists and logs.
settings.space_management_desc: Monitor and clean web proxies to free up disk space.
settings.metadata_apis_desc: Configure API keys for TMDB, OMDB and TVMaze.
settings.branding_assets_desc: Upload logos, fallback images and videos.
settings.playout_tab_intro: Configure the playout engine and quality presets.
settings.basic_config_desc: Set day start, channel name, FPS and encoding.
settings.epg_config_desc: Configure EPG distribution and number of days.
settings.overlay_config_desc: Configure logo, position, opacity and overlay scale.
settings.quality_presets_desc: Quickly select 720p, 1080p or 4K with optimized settings.
settings.user_management_desc: Add, delete users and change passwords.
settings.profile_management_desc: Create and edit profiles with custom permissions.
settings.about_tab_intro: System information, version history and product roadmap.
settings.system_info_desc: Version, last update and deployment environment.
settings.product_roadmap_desc: Implemented and planned features for the future.
settings.how_to_intro: Follow these steps to configure the system effectively:
settings.step1: Access the Settings menu in the sidebar
settings.step2: In the "Output" tab, select the protocol and configure resolution
settings.step3: In the "Paths & Media" tab, define storage directories
settings.step4: Configure metadata APIs (TMDB, OMDB) for automatic enrichment
settings.step5: In the "Playout" tab, adjust playout engine settings
settings.step6: In the "Users" tab, create profiles and users with appropriate permissions
settings.step7: Click "Save Changes" to apply all settings
settings.tips_content:
• Save settings after each change to avoid data loss
• Use quality presets for quick and optimized configuration
• Configure regular backups of storage paths
• Monitor disk space in the Space Management section
• Create user profiles with minimum necessary permissions
• Regularly check version history for updates
• Test connection links after changing protocol settings

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.intro: Solutions for the most common issues.

liveInputs.title: Live Inputs
liveInputs.intro: The Live Inputs module allows you to configure incoming video and audio streams for live broadcasting. This feature enables your playout system to accept external live sources and distribute them to your audience.

howToUse.title: How to Use
howToUse.intro: Follow these steps to set up a live input:
howToUse.step1: Click the "+ Add Input" button to create a new input.
howToUse.step2: Fill in the Input Name, select a Protocol (RTMP, SRT, UDP, WebRTC, NDI), and enter the Stream URL/Port.
howToUse.step3: If required, provide a Stream Key (e.g., for RTMP).
howToUse.step4: Optionally, set a Preview URL for HLS playback.
howToUse.step5: Save the input; it will appear in the list with its current status.
howToUse.step6: To start the stream, click the Play icon; to stop, click the Stop icon.

protocols.title: Supported Protocols
protocols.intro: The system supports multiple protocols for different use cases:
protocols.rtmp: RTMP (Real-Time Messaging Protocol) - Ideal for social media platforms like YouTube and Facebook. Requires a stream key. Port: 1935.
protocols.srt: SRT (Secure Reliable Transport) - High reliability streaming over unstable networks with error recovery and low latency. Port: 9000.
protocols.udp: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) - Lowest latency for local networks, but no retransmission. Use for IP encoders and local distribution. Port: 1234.
protocols.webrtc: WebRTC - Browser-based real-time communication, ideal for web-based live sources and low-latency browser streaming.
protocols.ndi: NDI (Network Device Interface) - Professional IP video workflow, ideal for studio environments and networked video sources.
protocols.sdi: SDI (Serial Digital Interface) - Traditional broadcast standard for direct video connections via capture cards.

socialStreaming.title: Social Streaming
socialStreaming.intro: Stream directly to social media platforms using the Social Streaming tab:
socialStreaming.youtube: YouTube Live - Requires stream key from YouTube Studio. Use RTMP protocol with rtmp://a.rtmp.youtube.com/live2.
socialStreaming.facebook: Facebook Live - Requires stream key from Facebook Page. Use RTMP protocol with rtmp://rtmp-api.facebook.com:1935/rtmp/.
socialStreaming.management: Manage social streams in the Social Streaming tab. Start/Stop streams directly from the interface and monitor status in real-time.

statusMonitoring.title: Status Monitoring
statusMonitoring.intro: Real-time status indicators help you monitor your streams:

preview.title: Preview Functionality
preview.intro: Set a Preview URL to see your stream in the application:
preview.hls: HLS preview URLs work best (m3u8 format). The system generates HLS previews automatically for local sources.
preview.latency: Note: Preview has inherent latency (6-10 seconds for HLS, sub-second for SRT/WebRTC).
preview.local: For local sources, use http://localhost:8080/hls/stream.m3u8 or similar.

tips.title: Tips & Best Practices
tips.content:
• Use SRT for unreliable networks; it provides error recovery and low latency.
• For local networks, UDP offers the lowest latency but lacks retransmission.
• Ensure the server firewall allows inbound connections on the configured ports (1935 for RTMP, 9000 for SRT, 1234 for UDP).
• Monitor the status chip: green (active), orange (connecting), red (error).
• You can edit or delete an input at any time via the icons in the card.
• For social streaming, use the dedicated Social Streaming tab for better management.
• Always test your stream before going live.
• Keep stream keys secure and rotate them regularly.
• Use descriptive names for easy identification.
• For NDI sources, ensure all devices are on the same network subnet.
• WebRTC requires HTTPS in production environments.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
items: Connection failed: Check URL, port, and firewall settings
Stream key invalid: Verify the key from the platform's dashboard
No preview: Ensure the preview URL is accessible and in HLS format
High latency: Consider using SRT instead of HLS for lower latency
Audio issues: Check codec compatibility and audio levels
Port already in use: Check if another service is using the configured port
NDI not detected: Verify NDI tools are installed and network allows multicast

tips.title: Tips & Best Practices
tips.content:
• Monitor System Score daily
• Keep at least 20% disk space free
• Check live diagnostics logs regularly
• NTP sync must be active for broadcast
• Manually refresh page if data doesn't update
• WebSocket must be connected for real-time analytics
• Check content availability before important broadcasts

Low score: Check components with error or warning status.
WebSocket disconnected: Refresh page or check network connection.
Low disk space: Delete old media or expand storage.
Database errors: Restart service or contact support.

templates.title: Templates
templates.intro: The Templates system allows you to create, manage, and reuse playlist structures for efficient broadcast scheduling.
templates.features_intro: The Template Generator provides powerful tools for content structuring:
templates.feature1: Pre-configured templates for common broadcast scenarios (morning shows, 24/7 programming, etc.)
templates.feature2: Custom template creation with flexible duration and block composition
templates.feature3: Template library with preset structures that can be quickly adapted
templates.feature4: One-click playlist generation from any template
templates.feature5: Block-based architecture (Intro, Content, Commercial, Outro, Filler)
templates.presets_intro: The system includes three ready-to-use preset templates:
templates.preset_morning_desc: A 6-hour template designed for morning programming (06:00-12:00) with structured content blocks and breaks.
templates.preset_full_day_desc: A complete 24-hour template with continuous content and a 1-hour filler buffer for scheduling flexibility.
templates.preset_loop_desc: A repeating 24-hour template with content blocks and commercial breaks, ideal for continuous looping programming.
templates.structure_intro: Templates are composed of sequential blocks that define the programming flow:
templates.block_intro_desc: Opening segment (typically 30 seconds) used for show introductions, station IDs, or opening credits.
templates.block_content_desc: Main programming block containing actual video content. Duration varies based on show format.
templates.block_commercial_desc: Advertising or break segment. Used for commercial spots, station identification, or public service announcements.
templates.block_outro_desc: Closing segment (typically 30 seconds) for show endings, credits, or station sign-offs.
templates.block_filler_desc: Emergency or buffer content used to fill gaps in the schedule. Automatically inserted when needed.
templates.create_intro: Follow these steps to create a custom template:
templates.create_name_desc: Enter a descriptive name that identifies the template's purpose (e.g., "Monday Morning News").
templates.create_description_desc: Add a brief explanation of when and how to use this template.
templates.create_duration_desc: Set the total length in seconds. For 24-hour templates, enter 86400 seconds.
templates.use_intro: Generate a playlist from any template in a few steps:
templates.use_select_desc: Choose a template from the Templates page by clicking the "USE" button.
templates.use_name_desc: Enter a unique name for the generated playlist (e.g., "Morning Show - March 20").
templates.use_date_desc: Select the date when this playlist will be scheduled in the Calendar.
templates.how_to_intro: Here's the complete process from template creation to broadcast:
templates.step1: Access the Templates page from the sidebar menu
templates.step2: Browse existing templates or create a new one with "CREATE TEMPLATE"
templates.step3: Define template structure with appropriate blocks and durations
templates.step4: Save the template for future use
templates.step5: When needed, click "USE" on any template to generate a playlist
templates.step6: The generated playlist appears in the Playlists section ready for scheduling
templates.tips_content:
• Create templates for recurring programming patterns (daily shows, weekly specials)
• Use descriptive names that include duration and purpose
• Include filler blocks in templates for scheduling flexibility
• Test templates by generating sample playlists before using them on air
• Keep template durations realistic (avoid over-scheduling)
• Update templates periodically based on programming changes
• Use the 24-hour template as a starting point for custom variations
• Remember that generated playlists can be further edited in the Playlist Editor

roadmap.title: PRODUCT ROADMAP
roadmap.intro: The following phases define the planned evolution of Cloud Onepa Playout beyond its current ALPHA state. No implementation has started — this is the strategic vision.
roadmap.note: These features are planned but not yet implemented. Custom categories (Rock, Salsa, Merengue, Jazz, Pop, etc.) will be available from Phase 32 onwards.

p32.title: CATEGORY FOLDERS & BATCH PLAYLIST
p32.desc: Organise media by genre/category and drag entire folders to playlists at once.
p32.item1: Category System: Full CRUD for default categories (Rock, Salsa, Merengue, Jazz, Pop, Reggaeton, Classical, News, Movies, Sports, Filler) + custom categories
p32.item2: Categories View: Visual grid in Media Library with file count per category
p32.item3: Drag Category → Playlist: Drop an entire folder to add all files at once (sequential or random)
p32.item4: Category Filter: Sidebar filter in Media Library and Playlist Editor

p33.title: LIVE SOURCE SWITCHING & NDI
p33.desc: Switch between live sources in real-time using broadcast-grade NDI networking.
p33.item1: NDI Input/Output: FFmpeg integration with NDI SDK for ultra-low-latency broadcast networks
p33.item2: Live Switcher UI: A/B preview component to switch sources in real-time with crossfade
p33.item3: Multi-Source PIP: Picture-in-Picture for sign language, inserts and breaking news

p34.title: AUDIO COMPLIANCE & MULTI-TRACK
p34.desc: Broadcast-grade EBU R128 audio normalisation and independent audio tracks.
p34.item1: EBU R128 Loudness: FFmpeg loudnorm filter per channel, compliant with satellite/cable standards
p34.item2: Multi-Audio Track: Independent tracks (Original + Audio Description + Multilingual)
p34.item3: Audio Metering UI: Real-time VU Meters and LUFS on the Dashboard via WebSocket

p35.title: AUTOMATED QC & INGEST VALIDATION
p35.desc: Automatic quality control on media import to prevent on-air failures.
p35.item1: Native QC: Automatic validation (black frames, freeze, silent audio, incompatible codec)
p35.item2: Smart Thumbnails: Intelligent representative frame extraction (not first frame)
p35.item3: Auto Proxy Generation: Automatic lightweight proxy creation for instant library preview

p36.title: FAST CHANNELS & MONETISATION
p36.desc: FAST channel delivery and dynamic ad insertion for revenue generation.
p36.item1: FAST Channel Delivery: Packaging for Pluto TV, Samsung TV Plus and FAST platforms
p36.item2: Dynamic Ad Insertion (DAI): SCTE-35 expansion for server-side insertion into LL-HLS
p36.item3: Viewer Analytics: Per-channel audience estimation and engagement metrics

p37.title: ENTERPRISE HARDENING
p37.desc: High availability, BXF compliance, RBAC and remote monitoring for broadcast operations.
p37.item1: Active-Active Redundancy: Heartbeat between playout instances with automatic failover
p37.item2: BXF/Traffic Integration: Import/export in Broadcast eXchange Format
p37.item3: Granular RBAC: Per-channel and per-feature role-based permissions
p37.item4: Remote Monitoring Dashboard: Read-only web interface for remote monitoring

p38.title: REDESIGN UI/UX (BROADCAST GRADE)
p38.desc: New professional interface focused on extreme productivity and master control aesthetics.
p38.item1: Design Tokens: Neon color palette and 'Deep Night' dark mode for 24/7 operating environments
p38.item2: Modularization: Lightweight and decoupled components for instant loading
p38.item3: Accessibility: Audited contrast and full keyboard navigation support

p39.title: PERFORMANCE HARDENING & VM STABILITY
p39.desc: Severe optimizations for limited hardware and extreme stability in VM environments.
p39.item1: Memory Management: PWA Caching and active memory purge in virtual components
p39.item2: Database Optimization: Connection pool reduction and instant queries for limited I/O
p39.item3: System Guard: Active resource monitoring and kernel limits adjusted for playout

p40.title: CG & LOGO ENGINE — BROADCAST CHARACTER GENERATOR
p40.desc: Complete redesign of the CG system and creation of a dedicated GPU-first Logo Engine microservice, fully isolated from the playout.
p40.item1: Logo Engine (C++ + GPU): Static VRAM texture, zero idle CPU, SET/HIDE/FADE/REPOSITION commands via IPC
p40.item2: Asset Pipeline (7 phases): Upload → Validation → Normalization → Optimization → Padding → Manifest → Deploy in < 10s
p40.item3: CG Engine (CEF/headless): HTML5+CSS3+JSON templates, layer system 0–4, max 2 visible layers, ≤2ms/frame composition
p40.item4: Control API + UI: REST + WebSocket + Prometheus metrics, drag & drop management, EBU R95 safe area, 1-click rollback
